failure_reason: Live site is behind Akamai Bot Manager ("Access Denied" edge deny, injected JS challenge script) that returned HTTP 403 on essentially every request path (/, /browse/*, /sitemap.xml, /product/*) across a 5-profile curl_cffi impersonation sweep (safari184_ios, safari18_0_ios, chrome131, chrome120, chrome124) repeated 15-25x per URL, plus WebFetch (403), r.jina.ai (blocked by its own Cloudflare challenge on this target), and translate.goog (HTTP 400, origin refused Google's fetcher). Only /robots.txt and one lucky homepage hit (1/25 tries) ever returned 200 live; every /browse/ category page failed 100% of ~150 combined attempts. Category structure and exact counts were instead recovered from recent (Jan-Jun 2026) Wayback Machine snapshots of each category page's Next.js SSR JSON (productsInCategory field) via the CDX API, which was independently reachable. Because those numbers are 1.5-7 months stale relative to today (2026-08-13) and not the live site's current report, every qty is set to null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag citing the Wayback reference count so a human/next pass can re-verify live once the block lifts.
notes: ACCESS: argos.co.uk is Akamai-protected; robots.txt (no Claude-specific disallow) was the only endpoint that reliably returned 200. All content paths (/, /browse/*, /sitemap.xml, /product/*) returned Akamai 'Access Denied' edge-deny pages (with an injected Bot Manager challenge script) on effectively every attempt across a 5-profile curl_cffi sweep x15-25 tries per URL, WebFetch, r.jina.ai, and translate.goog (400, origin refuses Google's fetcher). A single homepage fetch succeeded live (safari18_0_ios, try 5 of 25) and yielded the mega-menu taxonomy (window.__INITIAL_HEADER_STATE__), used to identify the two department nav nodes 'Home & Furniture' (/browse/home-and-furniture/c:29351/) and 'Garden & DIY' (/browse/garden-and-diy/c:797660/) that stand in for a unified 'Home & Garden' nav on this general UK catalogue retailer, per the scoping instruction. SIDE DOOR: web.archive.org was reachable via the same curl_cffi route; its CDX API and id_-suffixed snapshot URLs served each category page's Next.js SSR JSON (categoryData / categoryChildrenData / categoryData.relationships.children.data), which carries an exact productsInCategory integer per node -- the same field the live site would render as the count. Snapshots used range 2026-01-28 to 2026-06-07 (cited per-row in evidence/flag). SCOPE: extracted only from Home & Furniture's Lighting, Home Furnishings > Decorative Accessories / Candles & Candle Holders, Tableware, and Bathroom Accessories nodes, plus Garden & DIY's 'Garden Decor & Lighting' / 'Garden Decoration' nodes (outdoor lighting, garden pots & planters, garden ornaments, garden clocks, garden water features) -- not the whole site (Bedroom/Living Room/Dining/Kitchen furniture, Storage, Office, Laundry/Cleaning/Pets, DIY/tools/power tools, Painting & Decorating incl. wallpaper, Electrical Supplies, Home Security, Car Care were all out of scope and skipped). EXCLUSIONS applied: Light bulbs and the 'Smart lighting' hub (predominantly smart bulbs/kits, cross-listed under Technology > Smart Home Technology) dropped as bulb/wiring tech, not fixtures; the general 'Candles' bucket (349 items) dropped as an unverifiable scented/unscented mixed roll-up (WebSearch confirmed both scented Yankee Candle/Firefly SKUs and unscented Habitat/Argos Home SKUs share the one category with no facet split) while 'Candle Holders' (holder, not wax) was kept; Rugs, Cushions, Bean bags, Door mats, Blankets & throws, Draught excluders, Table linen, Outdoor cushions/rugs dropped as textiles; Christmas decorations/homewares dropped as Holiday & Gift; Artificial flowers/plants/trees (indoor and garden) dropped per explicit scope exclusion; Bird feeders/baths/houses dropped as functional garden wildlife items, not decor; Lunch boxes, Water bottles, Cutlery, Cafetieres, Travel mugs, and the mixed 'Outdoor dinnerware and cutlery' / 'Kids tableware and cutlery' roll-ups dropped (cutlery/consumable-adjacent, not separable from dinnerware -- 'Mixed roll-ups: drop, don't pad'); Bathroom scales, Toilet seats, Shower curtains, Towel rails & rings, Shower/bath storage, Toilet roll holders, Bathroom bins, Toilet brushes dropped as plumbing/fixtures/storage; Garden fencing/trellis, Decking, Garden edging, Garden arches, Pergolas, Garden gates dropped as landscaping structures/hardware, not decor. DEDUP within taxonomy: 'Bathroom lights' and 'Bathroom mirrors' each appear under two menu paths (Lighting hub and Bathroom Accessories hub; Mirrors hub and Bathroom Accessories hub) with matching counts -- kept once under the Lighting/Mirrors canonical path, dropped the Bathroom Accessories duplicate. A legacy 'Garden Mirrors' node (c:29417, indexed by Google under an old /browse/home-and-garden/... URL, last live Wayback snapshot 2017) no longer appears in the current (2026-03) Garden Decoration/Landscaping subtree -- retired/merged, most likely into 'Garden Ornaments'; not re-added as a separate row (Rule 0 'all mirrors in scope' is still satisfied by the six Mirrors-hub subtypes). DUPLICATE-COMPANY CHECK: grepped the project's json_archive for 'argos' -- only hit is c48.json (Habitat UK, habitat.co.uk), a Sainsbury's/Argos-group sibling brand documented there as running its own live storefront on its own domain (shared Akamai platform, x-argos-brand:hab header, a few Argos Home-branded SKUs) but a genuinely separate catalogue -- not a duplicate of Argos Home. No prior extraction of argos.co.uk itself exists in the archive.
